llm.summary: The package appears to be a genuine cross-platform social autoposter, but contains multiple internal inconsistencies (missing declared env-vars, a referenced uploader module that is not present in the manifest, and an optional Cloudflare R2 upload that contradicts the 'no third-party' claim), so proceed with caution and verify before installing or giving credentials.

dimensions.detail: The skill's code and SKILL.md clearly implement posting to X, Instagram, YouTube and Meta (consistent with its description). However the registry metadata claims 'Required env vars: none' and 'Required config paths: none' while SKILL.md and code require many platform credentials (X/Twitter keys, Instagram/Meta tokens, YouTube client_secrets.json) — that mismatch is an incoherence the user should notice.

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read a local content CSV and post autonomously to multiple platforms (expected). But it also claims 'No data is sent to any third-party service other than the platforms you configure' while the code includes Cloudflare R2 configuration and an upload step (instagram_main imports upload_to_r2). If R2 is enabled the skill will send generated videos to a third-party storage endpoint, contradicting the README/SKILL.md promise.

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec) and uses standard Python packages (moviepy, numpy, Pillow, tweepy, html2image). That's a typical footprint. There are no external download URLs in the manifest. Still, heavy native dependencies (moviepy, headless rendering) may require additional system packages when actually installed.

dimensions.detail: The skill requests many sensitive credentials (Twitter/X API keys, Instagram Graph tokens and app secret, Meta page token/ID, YouTube client_secrets.json) which are appropriate for posting but the registry metadata does not declare them — a mismatch. Additionally ig_config exposes optional Cloudflare R2 env vars (R2_ENDPOINT, R2_ACCESS_KEY, R2_SECRET_KEY) which, if set, will upload generated videos to that storage; this is a third-party exfiltration vector not clearly emphasized in SKILL.md's 'no third-party' claim.

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and uses normal autonomous invocation defaults. It does not appear to modify other skills or system-wide settings. The agent will be able to run it autonomously (platform default), which is expected for an autoposter; combine this with the credential concerns when deciding whether to enable autonomous runs.

llm.guidance:
This skill implements real posting functionality but has several red flags you should resolve before use:

- Do not provide high-privilege tokens until you confirm the code you will run. The registry metadata incorrectly lists no required env vars; SKILL.md and the code actually need many credentials (X/Twitter, Instagram, Meta, and YouTube client_secrets.json).
- Inspect or request the missing referenced module: instagram_main imports bot.r2_uploader (upload_to_r2) but that file is not present in the manifest you provided. Confirm whether the uploader exists and what it does before enabling R2-related env vars.
- Be aware that if you set Cloudflare R2 env vars the skill will upload generated videos to that bucket (a third-party service). That contradicts the SKILL.md statement 'No data is sent to any third-party service other than the platforms you configure.' If you don't want uploads to external storage, leave R2 env vars unset and verify local-only behavior via dry-run.
- Test in dry-run mode and with least-privilege accounts: use test social accounts and tokens with limited permissions, and run with --dry-run first to verify outputs without posting.
- Review branding and CTA code (strings referencing 'Mission UPSC' and Playstore). The skill appears tuned for a specific niche and includes promotional text; check/replace BRAND_URL and BRAND_NAME if you don't want implicit promotion.
- If you plan to enable autonomous posting, consider running the skill in an isolated environment (separate service account and credentials), audit network traffic, and review any omitted/truncated files before granting access to production accounts.

If you want, I can: (1) search the remaining truncated files for r2_uploader or other surprising behavior, (2) produce a short checklist of env vars and a safe test plan, or (3) point out exact lines to change to remove R2 uploading and branding.
